Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo. Our InfoSec team has a short follow-up on data custody and deletion timelines for hosted deployments. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's Hosted API?

1) Where request/response payloads and embeddings are stored geographically (primary region and any backups/replicas).
2) Default retention window for request logs, model inputs/outputs, and any derived embeddings.
3) How deletion is effected end-to-end (immediate wipe vs background job; timeline for caches, backups, and audit logs).
4) If data can be scoped to a single region (no cross-region replication) for a customer in the US.
5) Is there a mechanism to trigger an immediate purge for a customer (e.g., a tenant erasure request)? If so, what are the SLAs and limitations?

We'd like short, concrete answers we can paste into our questionnaire. If you need a vendor questionnaire template, I can attach one.

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Answers below are scoped to Redwood Hosted API (not Dedicated/Private). I kept each answer short so you can paste into your questionnaire; happy to expand on any bullet.

1) Geographic storage:
- Primary: customer requests and generated outputs are stored in the customer's selected AWS region (we currently support us-west-2 and us-east-1 for US-hosted tenants).
- Backups/replicas: automated snapshots are retained within the same AWS region by default; cross-region replication is off unless explicitly enabled via an enterprise contract.

2) Default retention windows:
- Request logs (trace metadata): 90 days (used for debugging/monitoring).
- Model inputs/outputs and ephemeral caches: 30 days by default; can be reduced via tenant settings.
- Generated embeddings: 30 days by default; customers can opt-in to longer retention for index-building.

3) Deletion mechanics:
- Erasure request: submitted via support portal or API -> creates a high-priority job.
- Runtime caches/kv: cleared within minutes after the job; we invalidate prefix caches and drop KV shards immediately.
- Persistent storage & snapshots: deletion jobs mark objects for removal and trigger background purge workers; full removal from all service-level storage typically completes within 72 hours, but final removal from backups/snapshots can take up to 30 days depending on snapshot schedule.
- Audit logs: immutable audit trails (access logs) are retained for compliance windows; per-customer access logs are redacted for PII on erasure but retained as event records for 90 days.

4) Single-region scoping:
- Yes — by default Hosted API tenants are provisioned in a single customer-selected region; we can guarantee no cross-region replication for customers who require geo-containment under standard hosted terms.

5) Immediate purge option & SLA: 
- We support an expedited tenant erasure API with a 72-hour SLA to complete logical deletion and cache invalidation.
- Physical cleanup from backups/snapshots: best-effort up to 30 days.
- Limitations: if a customer has activated managed replication or long-term snapshot exports (e.g., to S3 export buckets), those external exports must be removed per the export target's lifecycle (we assist customers to coordinate).

If useful, I can have Kim attach a short diagram of the purge flow and backup timing.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of technical clarifications / operational notes for Novaplan's runbook: 

- Snapshot cadence & retention specifics: automated nightly snapshots (region-local) kept for 30 days, with weekly promoted snapshots retained for 90 days. Deletion requests will mark snapshots for expedited removal; we estimate ~7–30 day window for complete snapshot tombstoning depending on where the snapshot is queued.

- Logs & monitoring exports: if you enable long-term exports to your own S3 or SIEM, those are subject to your export bucket lifecycle (we do not automatically delete customer export buckets). Recommend we jointly document any cross-account exports in the MSP addendum.

- Cache eviction: runtime prefix caches and KV shards are dropped immediately; ephemeral GPU KV caches are zeroed and reclaimed within the next allocation cycle (typically minutes).

- Evidence & audit: attached two short artifacts you can include with your questionnaire: hosted-data-purge-flow.pdf (diagram + timeline) and s3-snapshot-retention.txt (exact snapshot retention table).

Hi Sara — following up with the attachments Kimberly provided and a short confirmatory statement you can paste into your questionnaire: 

"Redwood Inference (Hosted API) stores customer request/response data in the customer-selected AWS region. By default we retain request logs for 90 days and inputs/outputs and generated embeddings for 30 days. Customers may reduce retention via tenant settings or enable longer retention for embeddings if they intend to build persistent indexes. Tenant erasure requests submitted via Redwood's support portal or our erasure API will invalidate runtime caches immediately and begin background deletion of persisted objects; logical deletion completes within 72 hours and final removal from snapshots/backups completes within 30 days in standard operations. Cross-region replication is not enabled by default. For customers requiring stricter containment, we offer single-region guarantees under our hosted terms and will document any managed exports during onboarding."
